niche: a cloud backup provider's posterior predictive forecast of quarterly drive replacements across three data centres, one acquired mid-life with its early failures unrecorded and its worst old vaults already retired
analyst_test: The careful but hurried review fits each drive family's age-hazard on every vault's history, dates the acquired centre's drives from their migration, reads the ramping batch as its family's trailing rate and puts Poisson bands around the sum, so it under-forecasts the acquired centre and the hot batch, over-forecasts the surviving old vaults, and gives bands that would have covered about four quarters in ten.
domain_test: Forecasting replacements as a posterior predictive count from a hierarchical hazard model (age, batch and vault effects pooled partially, lifetimes truncated at an acquisition and thinned by selective retirement, a defect batch's accelerating hazard, shocks shared within a chassis) is the reliability statistician's own work; swap in patients or subscribers and the vaults, chassis shocks, health-pull policy and spare lead time stop making sense.

driver: The decisive quantities are next year's failures in a fleet whose records start mid-life at one acquired site and whose worst units were retired first, a manufacturing batch whose hazard is accelerating, and intervals that carry the units' shared shocks; read with ages from first sight, a family's pooled history and independent counts, the forecast runs low where the units are older than recorded and where the batch ramps, high where the bad units have left, and its bands cover a fraction of what they claim.
driver_concrete: Halden Vault orders spare drives a quarter ahead: DC-3's Kestrel drives were installed years before the 2024 migration that sets their recorded install date and have no power-on hours, so their ages come from the serial's manufacture week; one HX-8 batch on old firmware has a hazard doubling every few months; operations retired the worst OM-6 vaults first, so the survivors are better than the family's pooled history; and chassis power and cooling events cluster failures, so Poisson bands are far too narrow.
stump: The careful but hurried review dates the acquired centre's drives from migration, reads the ramping batch at its family's trailing rate, pools the old family's history across the vaults operations retired first and puts Poisson bands on the sum, so its fleet total runs low by about a fifth inside bands a few per cent wide that would have covered about four quarters in ten, its spare order runs short and it keeps the hot-batch vaults in service (figures from the build).
results: R1 DC-3's replacements over the four quarters (ages rebuilt from serials); R2 the hot batch named with its current annualized rate; R3 the hot batch's four-quarter replacements with its doubling time; R4 the surviving OM-6 vaults' forward rate and count; R5 the fleet's quarterly path; R6 its 80% bands; R7 the back-test coverage of intervals built the same way over the four quarters to 30 September 2026; R8 the Q4 spare order per family and the migrate call with its flip point
